items.title: Position-aware layout model that drives the physics
items.why: GROUP B. DONE. sabes/layout/ holds two coordinate systems that never mix: `display` (Node.x/y/angle, Link.via) draws the table, `path_m` does the physics, and neither is derived from the other. A test pins that separation by showing the metres-per-display-unit ratio spans more than an order of magnitude across links -- a schematic has no single scale, which is precisely why reading distances off the drawing would have been wrong. Detection now asks the layout for cell->D-mirror and cell->lens instead of carrying `cell_to_dmirror_m` and `pd_lens_distance_m` as coefficients (both removed), and the crossing angle derives from the same measured 23 inch. beam_at(layout, x, y, chain) returns the beam at a point with its mode propagated TO that point, which is what makes a beam profiler on a long arm mean anything; it is the single input every virtual instrument will take. Two bugs were caught building it: stages were keyed by name alone, so the pump and seed arms -- both of which have a stage called 'at cell' -- collided and a probe on the pump reported the seed's power; and `Telescope.apply` collapsed the pair into one step, so a probe between L1 and L2 was handed the state from after the telescope (the beamline now records the intermediate). Results are unchanged, and the bridge in fact now reproduces a hand-driven GABES run to exactly zero at both Fast and Ultra. Still nominal, and worth measuring: D-mirror->iris (100 mm) and iris->lens (216 mm), which together set the photodiode spot.

items.title: Reconcile the seed path with the part 1 setup drawing
items.why: DONE, as part of sabes-layout-model. The part 1 drawing's Glan-Taylor after the etalon chain, the half-wave plate between etalons 1 and 2, and the distinct collimators (F230 pump, F220 seed) are all in the layout, along with the elements the physics still does not model but the table has: optical isolators, the MOPA's cylindrical lens, the seed-path noise eater, and the Rb-natural locking arm. Those are drawn and inert -- `Node.clickable` is true exactly when the physics owns a parameter, so 'clickable' and 'modelled' cannot drift apart. A test asserts every SetupSettings and DetectionSettings knob is owned by some optic, which is what Stage D needs in order to empty the sidebar without orphaning anything.

items.title: Bidirectional Streamlit canvas component: click -> Python
items.why: GROUP B. DONE, and the fallback is not needed. A hand-written bidirectional component works: sabes/components/canvas.py declares the component over a static frontend/index.html that implements the postMessage protocol (streamlit:componentReady / setFrameHeight / setComponentValue) in vanilla JS, with no npm, no lockfile and no build step -- it ships as package data. Verified against the running app at ?app=sabes&dev=canvas: the component loads and sizes its own frame; clicking an optic returns its id; clicking empty table returns a coordinate in SPEC units, checked at three different render scales including 0.42x, where a naive screen-pixel reading would have been wrong by more than a factor of two; and a repeat click on the same optic still re-fires, because Streamlit reruns only when a component value CHANGES and every event therefore carries a monotonic seq. One real bug was caught and fixed on the way: exporting the drawing function as `canvas` from the package __init__ shadowed the submodule of the same name, so it is now `svg_canvas`. CONFIRMED on Streamlit Community Cloud, which was the actual point of the spike: all four checks pass on the deployed app at ?app=sabes&dev=canvas, with the coordinate round-trip exact at the 1.06x render scale the deployment happens to use. Deployment also surfaced one thing local testing could not: Community Cloud wraps the app in a second same-origin iframe, so the browser-tab retitling reached only the wrapper and the real tab kept its old name -- the title observer now targets window.top rather than window.parent. Delete sabes/components/spike.py and its ?dev=canvas route once the table view lands.

items.title: Optical-table view reproducing the two setup drawings
items.why: GROUP B. DONE. sabes/layout/render.py turns a layout plus the live source chain into a canvas spec; sabes_page.py shows it as the first tab, one part at a time. Optics are drawn as glyphs built from sub-primitives inside a single clickable group (a polarizing cube is a square plus its diagonal, an etalon a plate plus its two faces), so a rich shape does not fragment into separate click targets. Glyph choice is matched on the id's own vocabulary rather than a per-node styling field, so adding an optic needs no renderer change and an unmatched node still draws. Two conventions are enforced by test: stroke width encodes POWER logarithmically and is not beam size (a 530 um beam on a metre of table is 0.05 percent of the width -- drawn honestly it would be invisible), and the legend says so; and shape clickability is exactly Node.clickable, so 'clickable' and 'modelled' cannot drift apart. Colours reuse the setup drawings' own key. Clicking an optic selects it and shows what it owns; clicking anywhere else drops a probe and reports the beam there via beam_at, with power, radius and the segment's provenance. Editing in place is Stage D. Three implementation findings worth keeping: (1) a component's value only reaches Python at the START of a run, so panels rendered after the canvas read the previous selection -- the handler now signals a rerun rather than letting the readout trail one click behind; (2) Streamlit does not re-lay-out a custom component that first mounts inside an inactive tab, so the second canvas stayed pinned at 300x0 -- the part selector is a radio, not nested tabs, which also halves the work per rerun; (3) the frontend now re-reports its height from a ResizeObserver instead of only on window resize. Placement is still a clean schematic in the drawings' arrangement rather than a pixel trace; refining it against the images is the remaining polish.

items.title: Click an optic to edit its parameters in a dialog
items.why: GROUP B. DONE, and the parameter-count problem is what it actually fixed. The 23-control sidebar is gone: clicking an optic on the drawing opens an st.dialog holding exactly the knobs that optic owns, and the sidebar now carries only the global controls (fidelity, Solve knobs, Reset, the link back to GABES) with ZERO number inputs. Control definitions moved from a sidebar-shaped list of groups to a `CONTROLS` registry keyed by parameter name, so the dialog and any remaining sidebar control render from one definition and cannot drift. A test asserts every entry in CONTROLS is owned by some optic on some layout -- a knob nothing claims would be unreachable now that the sidebar no longer lists them -- and the sidebar keeps an orphan fallback that a healthy build never enters. Side benefit delivered: per-etalon detuning. The model always accepted a 3-tuple and only the UI collapsed it; each stage now owns etalon_detune_ghz_{1,2,3} and detuning one stage alone changes seed power and carrier ratio independently, which matches a lab where each etalon has its own knob and temperature. Verified in-browser end to end: clicking the split half-wave plate opened its dialog, editing the angle to 20 deg moved the pump from 726 to 426 mW and the gain-referred diagnostic to -6.72 dB, and Done closed it. Note the click sets a session flag that survives the rerun the dialog needs, because a component value only reaches Python at the start of a run; the dialog clears the flag on close.

items.title: Virtual lab instruments driven by the real model
items.why: GROUP B. DONE. sabes/instruments/ holds power meter, beam profiler, wavemeter, photodiode, oscilloscope and spectrum analyser. Optical heads take whatever sabes.layout.beam_at resolves at a clicked point; the oscilloscope and analyser take a PhotocurrentSignal from a photodiode, so they cannot be pointed at a bare beam -- the right restriction rather than an inconvenience. A test asserts the package imports neither the layout nor streamlit nor matplotlib, so it stays liftable. The wavemeter is the demonstration piece: dropped either side of the etalon chain it shows carrier:wanted going 34.96 -> 4.18 -> 0.0596 percent, which is the whole reason the seed path has three filters. The power meter deliberately reports total AND wanted and warns when they differ, because a real power meter cannot tell them apart -- which is exactly why purity needs its own instrument. The profiler reports the 1/e^2 radius WHERE IT IS, not the waist; the two differ by a factor of two over a metre of table. One API fault was caught and fixed: the analyser took a total_power_w override for the shot-noise level (a balanced measurement sees both arms while the head is one diode) but read clearance off the signal, so the two could disagree silently. Clearance is now derived from the same power. Verified in the app: clicking the seed line after etalon 1 and switching instruments gives a power meter warning at 82.4 percent purity, a wavemeter reading 4.177 percent carrier, and an analyser with its SYNTHESISED badge reporting where the explicitly nonphysical gain-diagnostic overlay sits relative to the amplifier floor.

items.title: Return the dispersive partner of the OD/SAS absorption profile
items.problem: The OD/SAS spectrum is assembled from unit-area absorption Lorentzians only, so the real part of the susceptibility is never formed. Refractive index, accumulated phase, polarization rotation, and group index are unavailable on the one scheme that owns the validated hyperfine absolute scale, and any later polarimetric or Faraday/Voigt readout would have no dispersive input to propagate.
evidence: schemes/sas.py builds each hyperfine component as a unit-area Lorentzian (hwhm/pi)/(arg^2 + hwhm^2) and sums absorption only; observables.py exposes transmission and optical_density from alpha, while observables.group_index has no OD/SAS caller.

ElecSus obtains absorption and dispersion from a single Faddeeva evaluation of one complex line profile and reuses the real part for refractive index, rotation angle, and group index (libs/spectra.py, add_voigt).
items.why: DONE. Each hyperfine component now contributes one complex profile, chi_t = (A_t/k)*i/(pi*(Gamma_eff/2 - i*delta_t)): the imaginary part is the unit-area lineshape that already built alpha and the real part is its Kramers-Kronig partner, both weighted by the same velocity-resolved population difference and the same Doppler quadrature, so a pumped spectrum reports the saturated medium's dispersion. The generic path takes both quadratures from the one weak-probe susceptibility it already solved. compute() returns chi_real_unit and k_vec; observables scales it with the same line-strength factor as alpha and adds a Dispersion view (n - 1 in ppm, ASCII axis labels) plus a Peak phase shift metric. observables.refractive_index and observables.single_pass_phase now hold the dilute-vapor convention that group_index also calls. alpha is bit-for-bit unchanged on seven species/line/pump/coating cases checked against the previous revision, so the AutoOD anchor is untouched. Both quadratures agree with an independent scipy Faddeeva Voigt reference to 3e-4 at 25 C and 90 C, and the homogeneous-limit sign is pinned by a two-level OBE fixture (Re chi / Im chi = -delta/hwhm to 2e-8, n > 1 below resonance). No group-index readout is exposed.
acceptance_criteria: Absorption and dispersion for each hyperfine component come from one complex lineshape evaluation with a documented sign and frequency convention, not from two independently normalized profiles.

The dispersive component carries the same velocity-resolved population difference and the same Doppler quadrature as the absorption; a weak-probe dispersion is never paired with a saturated absorption spectrum.
A Kramers-Kronig or analytic-Voigt fixture checks the returned real part against an independent reference in both the homogeneous limit and a Doppler-broadened case.
The pump-off Rb-85 D1 AutoOD absolute anchor remains within its documented 0.1% tolerance.
Any refractive-index or group-index readout reuses observables.group_index instead of a scheme-local re-implementation, and states whether it is a phase or a group quantity.
out_of_scope: Polarization propagation and Stokes observables, which belong to od-sas-weak-probe-magneto-optical-reference-mode.
Changes to FWM susceptibility conventions or frozen FWM baselines.

items.title: Add a weak-probe Zeeman and polarization reference path for absorption spectra
items.problem: The OD/SAS manifold is hyperfine-lumped and its readout is a scalar absorption coefficient, so an applied magnetic field, an input polarization, and every polarimetric observable (Faraday rotation, dichroism, Stokes parameters) lie outside the model. Solving the full m_F manifold with the OBE for every velocity class and scan point costs far more than the weak-probe limit these measurements need.
evidence: schemes/sas.py declares no magnetic-field or polarization parameter and returns transmission and optical density from a scalar alpha.

The Zeeman machinery in zeeman.py serves the magneto scheme for a single 87Rb D1 F -> F' pair with a longitudinal field, so it does not cover a Doppler-broadened multi-line D1/D2 spectrum at arbitrary field magnitude and direction.
paraffin-coated-cell-extensions already records that the hyperfine-lumped OD/SAS manifold cannot carry Zeeman polarization moments.

ElecSus reaches the same physics in the weak-probe limit by diagonalizing the hyperfine plus Zeeman Hamiltonian in the uncoupled basis per isotope, which stays valid from the anomalous Zeeman regime through hyperfine Paschen-Back, then propagates the field through the dielectric-tensor normal modes and applies Jones matrices to obtain S0-S3 and the linear and circular intensities (libs/EigenSystem.py, libs/solve_dielectric.py, libs/spectra.py, libs/JonesMatrices.py).

Level energies and transition strengths come from one diagonalization valid at arbitrary field, with the low-field and Paschen-Back limits checked against independent references.
The ground-state population assumption is stated, degeneracy-weighted or Boltzmann, and is testable in a case with large ground-state splitting.

Polarization propagation uses the medium's normal modes rather than assuming a Faraday geometry; Voigt and intermediate angles are either supported with a convergence statement or refused with an explicit unsupported status.
Transmission, rotation, and ellipticity are all derived from one output field vector, so they cannot disagree with each other.

items.activation_trigger: Select a bounded collected-mode/filter model with measured geometry, overlap or transfer/leakage data and mode covariance or a justified physical source model. Reuse existing classical mode/RIN ledgers and establish fit/holdout data before adding new noise parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Separate atomic generation modes, collection overlap and post-cell mode-selective vacuum loss. Propagate matched-pair covariance and coherent/uncorrelated background/RIN through each stage with explicit correlations and no double-counted cell absorption.
Convert input carrier/seed ratios to per-detector SNL and excess-PSD fractions through their own gain/filter paths. Never use the cell-input ratio as the detected independent-background fraction.

Reproduce the independent coherent-mixture and pure-loss limits. The Jain comparison -7.2 dB plus exactly 10% symmetric vacuum loss -> -5.66244 dB is a fixture, while measured -4.4 dB is a separate residual requiring evidence, not another freely fitted scalar penalty.

Test source/covariance/detector cache separation: changing external filter/QE/weight does not rerun the atomic solve, while changing seed spectral content that drives atoms invalidates the appropriate source cache.

Compare held-out carrier-leakage and mode-coupling sweeps, including gold spectral-purity degradation and fiber input/output observations, with uncertainties and measured operating planes. Unsupported correlations remain unknown rather than inferred from total powers.

items.title: Calculate coupled operating regions, drift tolerance and shared noise budgets
items.problem: V7 demonstrates conditional connected intervals and finite distributed-model optima, but one-variable ranges cannot be combined into an independent tolerance box. Gain-only maps prefer the detection floor, and missing electronics/RIN/transport can produce unrealistically broad seed or geometry tolerances.
acceptance_criteria: Build a reusable analysis framework with typed objectives and provenance. V7 gain-conditioned and constant-coefficient Gaussian results are conditional fixtures; physical squeezing/bandwidth tolerances require the microscopic or measured covariance, RF readout, calibrated detection and their declared validation domain.

For a predeclared nominal point and common performance threshold, return connected fixed-control and retuned-control intervals/regions with root refinement. Store scan-edge censoring, nonfinite/unconverged regions, boundary minima and cap/floor dominance instead of publishing them as finite tolerances.
Track branch continuity and feasible retuning paths. A better point on a distant TPD branch is not automatically a continuously reachable lock trajectory.

Analyze OPD-TPD-pump light shift, P_p/w_p^2 with overlap/transit, N(T)L with absorption, angle-RF-scatter, seed-etalon-background and efficiency-weight-delay couplings. Report identifiable combinations rather than independent fitted coefficients when data cannot separate them.

Use one shared detected-noise budget for loss, background, seed/pump RIN and electronics; do not allow every single-variable maximum simultaneously. Distinguish numerical crossing accuracy from propagated model/measurement uncertainty and evaluate correlated drift with declared covariance/distributions.

Report target-IDS and target-RF-bandwidth achievement together, expected performance/stability under measured drift, and the active limiting variable. Apparatus-specific Allen ranges are comparison data, not universal gold tolerance.

Preserve v7 reproduction cases including fixed-TPD lower temperature 119.03656 C, pump 361.8439 mW and TPD connected interval [-18.40872,61.54507] MHz as conditional checks only; update physical conclusions when covariance/2D/transport replaces the original assumptions.

items.closeout_2026_11_17: ⟦AI⟧ D3 implemented in 8846193 with Exact Maxwell Voigt background and a 5-sigma pumped-minus-unpumped correction using a converged pump-state table. All 12 preregistered cases passed. Peak-normalized absorption/dispersion errors were 5.4713e-6/3.3999e-6, max transmission error 1.6464e-5 and zero-pump limit 1.5154e-7. Warm fresh-solve cost at most 1.936x and 204.54 MiB compiled; 4001-point NumPy fallback used 169.86 MiB. Legacy and old migrated settings reproduced 5659 leaves by bytes. Focused suite passed 273. Hot 87Rb D2 at 0.01 mW moved by -5.197 percentage points. Axial, coated, finite-probe, additional-species and other ineligible branches retain their prior measure.
items.user_decision_2026_11_17: User decision 2026-11-17: revisit the 2026-11-04 decision that kept the 1 m/s, ±4σ measure for pumped SAS (sas-od-dense-velocity-arithmetic). Remove the truncation from the default pumped path, either by widening the velocity window or by combining the Exact Voigt background with the grid-computed pump-induced change, whichever meets the reference at lower cost. ⟦AI⟧ Explicit Legacy and saved settings without a profile field keep replaying the ±4σ grid.
items.problem: ⟦AI⟧ The 2026-11-04 decision rested on the pump-off defaults, where the ±4σ cutoff leaves 1.9e-4 of the peak. b992d53 made Automatic use Exact Voigt at zero pump. Its reproduction case (pure 87Rb D2, 90 °C, 75 mm, zero pump and probe, 1,201 points) gives Legacy 71.65584 % and Exact 66.45873 % transmission at −1.400961020 GHz from the D2 centroid (−5.19712 percentage points; refined extremum 5.23601). The F=2→F′=3 resonance there lies at 4.053σ, outside the window; untruncated integration agrees with Exact to 6.18e-12. Pumped SAS keeps the ±4σ grid, so in optically thick cells its transmission is biased high and the smallest positive pump steps away from the zero-pump Exact curve by the same amount.
acceptance_criteria: ⟦AI⟧ Build an independent dense pumped-SAS reference (untruncated or widened velocity range with a converged step) over a matrix that includes the 90 °C 87Rb D2 75 mm case, the Rb D1/D2 defaults, cold and hot cells, and weak to saturating pump. Freeze the tolerance and cost budget before collecting evidence.

⟦AI⟧ As pump power goes to zero the default pumped result approaches the zero-pump Exact Voigt curve within 1e-6 absolute transmission (the OD budget decision), so the step at the mode boundary disappears.

⟦AI⟧ Fresh-solve time and memory stay within the OD budget decision (at most twice the previous time under the same conditions, 512 MiB). Explicit Legacy and old saved settings replay bit-identically. Pump comparisons use one measure for every sample.

⟦AI⟧ Own value commit citing this decision, with readout shifts at the defaults and in the hot case. Axial, coated-cell and finite-probe paths that share the grid either adopt the same measure or are listed with their remaining truncation.
